# Footer

The footer is the last element at the bottom of a scrollable page below the main content.

<Canvas of={FooterStories.Basic} />

## Examples

Custom CSS used in the following examples. Get carbon grid background image : [carbongrid.png](https://github.airbus.corp/Airbus/design-system/tree/develop/packages/design-tokens/assets/carbongrid.png)

```css
.carbongrid {
  background-image: url("./carbongrid.png");
}
.footer-maxwidth {
  width: 100%;
  max-width: calc(1440px - 2rem);
  margin: 0 auto;
}
.footer-secondary {
  max-width: calc(1440px - 3rem);
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  justify-content: center;
  gap: 1rem;
}
.footer-col {
  flex: 1;
  min-width: 120px;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  align-items: flex-start;
}
.footer-col h6 {
  margin-bottom: 1rem;
}
.footer-col a {
  margin-left: -0.5rem;
  margin-bottom: 1rem;
}
```

### Secondary links

Use the [carbon grid background](https://github.airbus.corp/Airbus/design-system/tree/develop/packages/design-tokens/assets/carbongrid.png) on secondary links to enforce Airbus branding.

Secondary content of the footer is free. This example show how to build a responsive footer with four columns of links and a maximum width of 1440px.

<Canvas of={FooterStories.Secondary} />

### Extended

Social links or any additional content can be displayed in secondary or extended parts of the footer.

<Canvas of={FooterStories.Extended} />

### Dark mode

<Canvas of={FooterStories.Dark} />

### Mobile

Apply the `ds-footer--mobile` modifier class on the `<footer>` element to switch to responsive mode of the primary footer. (secondary and extended content is up to you)

<Canvas of={FooterStories.Mobile} />

```css
.w-480 {
  width: 480px;
}
```
